Meta.title: CHEMVERSE AI — an AI platform for chemistry
Meta.description: A chemistry space for teachers and students: 3D and AR molecules, gesture control, a virtual lab, an AI tutor in Kazakh, and preparation for the UNT, MODO and olympiads.

Hero.lead: CHEMVERSE AI is a chemistry space for teachers and students: 3D and AR molecules, gesture control, a virtual lab, an AI tutor in Kazakh, and preparation for the UNT, MODO and olympiads — all in one place.

h2o.name: Water
h2o.description: The basis of life. Two lone pairs on oxygen bend the molecule, which makes water a polar solvent.

co2.name: Carbon dioxide
co2.description: A product of breathing and burning. Its two double bonds lie on one line, so the molecule is nonpolar.

ch4.name: Methane
ch4.description: The main component of natural gas. Four C–H bonds point to the corners of a tetrahedron.

nh3.name: Ammonia
nh3.description: A pungent gas and raw material for fertilizers. The lone pair on nitrogen gives the molecule a pyramid shape.

ethanol.name: Ethanol
ethanol.description: A typical alcohol. Its –OH group forms hydrogen bonds with water molecules.

benzene.name: Benzene
benzene.description: An aromatic hydrocarbon. The electrons of its six carbon atoms are spread evenly around the ring.

nacl.name: Sodium chloride (table salt)
nacl.description: An ionic compound: not a molecule but a crystal lattice of Na⁺ and Cl⁻ ions. Each ion is surrounded by 6 counter-ions.

h2so4.name: Sulfuric acid
h2so4.description: A strong diprotic acid and the key product of the chemical industry. Sulfur has an oxidation state of +6.

glucose.name: Glucose
glucose.description: A product of photosynthesis and the cell’s main energy source. In solution it exists mostly as a ring.

caffeine.name: Caffeine
caffeine.description: An alkaloid found in tea and coffee. A flat structure of two fused rings with four nitrogen atoms.

Modules.title: One platform — from lesson to exam
Modules.text: The teacher plans the lesson and runs a live quiz with the class; at home, students review with 3D and AI and prepare for the UNT. All results are stored in one place.

molecules.title: 3D molecules and AR
molecules.text: Rotate a molecule and tap an atom to see its properties. Scan a QR code in a textbook or on a slide, and the molecule appears on the desk through the phone camera.

gesture.title: Gesture control
gesture.text: The camera recognizes your hand: point to rotate, pinch to zoom, make a fist for the next molecule.

lab.title: Virtual lab
lab.text: Titration, pH and indicators even in a school without reagents. Dangerous experiments — done safely.

tutor.title: AI tutor in Kazakh
tutor.text: Step-by-step explanations with sources. A guiding mode helps without giving the answer away.

live.title: Live lesson
live.text: QR on the projector → students join from their phones → answers update the chart in real time.

plan.title: AI lesson plan
plan.text: Type a topic and get a short-term plan with learning objectives, assessment criteria and descriptors.

exams.title: UNT · MODO · Olympiad
exams.text: Timed tests, server-side grading, a map of weak topics and AI error analysis.

Lab.title: Titrating an acid with a base
Lab.text: The flask holds 25 mL of 0.1 M HCl with phenolphthalein. Add 0.1 M NaOH from the burette. pH is calculated with the exact formula: past the equivalence point, the solution turns raspberry pink.
Lab.curveLabel: Titration curve: pH versus the volume of NaOH added
Lab.conditions: HCl + NaOH → NaCl + H₂O · c(HCl) = c(NaOH) = 0.1 mol/L · phenolphthalein: colorless to raspberry pink at pH 8.2–10

Ai.title: Ask a question — get a step-by-step answer
Ai.text: The AI relies only on verified learning materials, and the program recalculates numerical answers to check them. Every answer ends with its source.
Ai.privacy: Camera frames are processed on the device and never sent to a server.

chat.title: Chemistry AI
chat.greeting: Hi! I’m your chemistry assistant. Pick one of the questions below and I’ll explain it step by step.

shape.q: Why is a water molecule bent?
shape.a:
1) The oxygen atom has 4 electron pairs around it: 2 bonding pairs and 2 lone pairs.
2) The four pairs point toward the corners of a tetrahedron.
3) Lone pairs repel the bonds more strongly, so the H–O–H angle is not 109.5° but about 104.5°.

Pick H₂O in the 3D viewer above and take a look.
shape.src: Source: Chemistry, grade 8, “Spatial structure of molecules”

ph.q: What is the pH of a 0.1 M HCl solution?
ph.a:
1) HCl is a strong acid and dissociates completely: HCl → H⁺ + Cl⁻.
2) So [H⁺] = 0.1 mol/L.
3) pH = −log[H⁺] = −log(0.1) = 1.

Check: the titration curve in the lab starts at exactly pH = 1.00 at 0 mL.

bonds.q: How do covalent and ionic bonds differ?
bonds.a:
Covalent bond: atoms share an electron pair (H₂O, CH₄, CO₂).
Ionic bond: an electron moves completely from one atom to another, and the oppositely charged ions attract each other (NaCl).

Remember: if the electronegativity difference is greater than about 1.7, the bond is mostly ionic.
bonds.src: Source: Chemistry, grade 8, “Types of chemical bonds”

Live.title: The whole class answers one question — in 30 seconds
Live.text: The teacher puts a QR code on the projector. Students join without signing up, using just their name. The chart updates with every answer, so you instantly see who didn’t get it.
Live.qrLabel: QR code to join the live lesson
Live.question: What is the shape of a methane (CH₄) molecule?

Studio.title: A short-term plan — in one minute
Studio.text: Choose a topic and the AI suggests lesson stages, timing, tasks and platform resources: 3D, the lab, QR. The teacher makes the final call: every plan is fully editable.
Studio.goalNote: Check the objective code against the current curriculum

bond.title: Types of chemical bonds
bond.goal: 8.2.2.1 — explain how covalent (polar, nonpolar) and ionic bonds form

items.1: Hook: “Why does table salt dissolve in water while fat doesn’t?”
Pair work: explore H₂O, CO₂ and NaCl models in 3D
items.2: Table: determine the bond type from the electronegativity difference
items.3: Differentiation: the advanced level compares NH₃ and CH₄

items.1: Formative assessment: 5 questions (auto-checked on the platform)
items.2: Reflection: “What I understood today / what was hard”

bond.criteria: Determines the bond type from electronegativity; gives two examples; shows the shared electron pair on a model.

acid.title: Acids and bases. pH
acid.goal: 8.3.1.3 — determine the medium of solutions using the pH scale and indicators

items.1: Predict the medium of household substances (lemon, soap)
Virtual lab: titrate an HCl solution with NaOH
items.2: Find the equivalence point on the curve and explain the indicator color change
items.3: Differentiation: pH calculation problems (0.1 M; 0.01 M)

items.2: Reflection: “Which substance at home would you like to know the pH of?”

acid.criteria: Identifies the medium from the pH value; explains the color change of phenolphthalein; calculates the pH of a strong acid.

mol.title: Spatial structure of molecules
mol.goal: 8.2.2.4 — explain the shape of molecules by electron pair repulsion

items.1: Problem question: “Why is CO₂ linear while H₂O is bent?”
Camera control: a student at the board rotates a molecule by hand
items.2: Group work: compare the angles in CH₄, NH₃ and H₂O
items.3: AR: see the molecule on the desk via the QR code in the homework

items.1: Live lesson: 3 questions with instant analysis of the results

mol.criteria: Names the shape of the molecule; explains the difference in angles by lone electron pairs.
